answer: A sybil swarm profits when berths are free, so admit only a fixed number of newcomers per epoch at the wharf, allocated by sealed cipher bids: each applicant commits a hidden bid, then reveals it to cross the bridge to established status. One operator spawning a thousand clones must bid against itself, driving the clearing price up for every berth it takes, while a lone genuine agent needs only one slot at the marginal price. Non-transferable berths and one reveal per committed bid make reselling or recycling slots useless, so scale itself becomes the attacker's bill.
